artboards.title: Real case · PHOTO tile · no mark
Nine covers as the profile grid

annotations.text:
THE SYSTEM v2 (Grow with Alex method → Golden Horseshoe Watch)

Three colours, each with a job: charcoal #17140F background · off-white #F2ECE0 primary · amber #D4A24C accent (one word per headline, numerals, rule line).

Two fonts: Anton display (headlines, numerals) + DM Sans body. Optional third: one brush word per slide, amber or off-white, only when it carries the emotion.

One layout, never rebuilt: eyebrow with the CITY · headline top zone · handle bottom-left · page count + arrow bottom-right · 80px margins on 1080×1350.

Palette and fonts are defaults until Alvin locks his own.

THE PLACE DOES THE NAMING

Every slide that isn't an explainer cover sits on a real Golden Horseshoe place, photographed in monochrome with one warm light. A Mississauga post sits on Mississauga. A Hamilton case sits on Hamilton. A province-wide stat sits on a GO platform or the CN Tower from the lake.

Black-and-white is what lets a photo obey the three-colour rule: it physically cannot smuggle a fourth colour in.

The dashed zones on these boards mark where the Higgsfield place plate drops in. Prompts and the city library: docs/signal-imagery.md.

THREE TILE TYPES

PHOTO — charcoal duotone place, off-white type, one amber word.
LIGHT — solid off-white, charcoal type, amber number or word.
ACCENT — solid amber, charcoal type, off-white or brush accent.

Same layout on all three; only the tile colour swaps. Covers are assigned a tile type when they enter the calendar so the profile grid alternates on purpose. See the Grid rhythm page.

MARK RULE
Raccoon detective + horseshoe glass on explainer / checklist / findings covers only. Never on a real case, never on a stat, never on a both-sides turn.

COPY STATUS
All legal copy here is draft. Run the sourcing pass (RTA / Tribunals Ontario) before anything posts. Bracketed text is a placeholder by design.

THE GRID TEST, DESIGNED

Alex: zoom out on your last nine posts. If the first three rows look intentional, you have a brand.

The LA reference does this by alternating black photo tiles, white solid tiles and orange solid tiles. We do the same with charcoal photo · off-white · amber.

Rule: never two LIGHT or two ACCENT covers in a row. The eyebrow on every tile names the city, and the photo behind it shows the city, so the grid reads as a map of the Golden Horseshoe before anyone reads a headline.
